questions.question_content: Which of the following is used to identify a specific device that is connected to the internet?
questions.explanation: Every device connected to the internet is identified by a unique IP address.

questions.question_content: In the website address varakumar.ccbp.tech, which of the following is the sub domain?
questions.explanation: The part before the domain name, here varakumar, is the sub domain; ccbp is the domain name and tech is the top-level domain.

questions.question_content: In the given code, src is an ___.
questions.explanation: src is written inside the start tag of the <img> element as name="value", so it is an HTML attribute.

questions.question_content: Which of the following is not an HTML attribute name?
questions.explanation: font-size is a CSS property; src, href and alt are HTML attributes.

questions.question_content:
Which of the following options is correct?
Statement-1: To curve the bottom right corner of an HTML element we use the CSS border-top-left-radius property.
Statement-2: To apply a background color to an HTML element we use the CSS background-color property.
questions.explanation: The bottom right corner is curved with border-bottom-right-radius, so Statement-1 is wrong; background-color sets the background color, so Statement-2 is right.

questions.question_content:
Which of the following options is correct?
Statement-1: To bold a text we can use the CSS property font-weight.
Statement-2: To add an overline to a text we can use the CSS property text-decoration.
questions.explanation: font-weight: bold makes text bold, and text-decoration: overline draws a line above the text, so both statements are correct.

questions.question_content:
A URL like `https://www.example.com/about/team` has three parts: the **protocol** (`https`), the **domain** (`www.example.com`) and the **path** (`/about/team`).

Given a URL, print its three parts. The protocol is everything before `://`. The domain is everything after `://` up to (not including) the first `/`. The path is everything from that `/` to the end. If there is no `/` after the domain, the path is `/`.

#### Input
A single line containing a URL. It always contains `://` and has no spaces.

#### Output
Three lines, exactly in this format:
```
Protocol: <protocol>
Domain: <domain>
Path: <path>
```

#### Sample Input
```
https://www.example.com/about/team
```

#### Sample Output
```
Protocol: https
Domain: www.example.com
Path: /about/team
```

When a browser requests a page, the server replies with a 3-digit HTTP status code. The first digit tells the class:

- `1xx` -> `Informational`
- `2xx` -> `Success`
- `3xx` -> `Redirection`
- `4xx` -> `Client Error`
- `5xx` -> `Server Error`

A code is valid only if it is made of exactly 3 digits and lies between 100 and 599 (inclusive). Anything else is `Invalid`.

For each code print its class, then print how many valid codes were errors (4xx or 5xx).

#### Input
The first line contains an integer `N` (1 <= N <= 50).
Each of the next `N` lines contains one code (a string without spaces, which may be invalid).

#### Output
`N` lines in the form `<code>: <class>` (print the code exactly as given), followed by one line `Errors: E`.

#### Sample Input
```
4
200
404
301
500
```

#### Sample Output
```
200: Success
404: Client Error
301: Redirection
500: Server Error
Errors: 2
```

questions.question_content:
When you open a URL, the browser sends an HTTP request that starts with a **request line** and a **Host** header. Given a method and a URL, build these lines and also break the host name into its parts.

Rules:
1. Convert the method to uppercase.
2. If the URL contains `://`, remove everything up to and including `://`.
3. The **host** is the text up to (not including) the first `/` or `?` (whichever comes first); convert it to lowercase. The **target** is the rest of the text (keep its case). If the target is empty, it is `/`. If the target starts with `?`, put `/` in front of it.
4. Split the host by `.`: the last label is the **TLD**, the label before it is the **domain**, and all labels before that (joined with `.`) form the **subdomain**. If there are no such labels, the subdomain is `none`.

#### Input
The first line contains the method (e.g. `get`, `POST`).
The second line contains the URL (no spaces, no port number). The host always has at least two labels (e.g. `ccbp.in`).

#### Output
Five lines, exactly in this format:
```
<METHOD> <target> HTTP/1.1
Host: <host>
Subdomain: <subdomain>
Domain: <domain>
TLD: <tld>
```

#### Sample Input
```
get
https://varakumar.ccbp.tech/about
```

#### Sample Output
```
GET /about HTTP/1.1
Host: varakumar.ccbp.tech
Subdomain: varakumar
Domain: ccbp
TLD: tech
```
